title: ASCEND IT & Networking Foundations Knowledge Check
lmsTitle: ASCEND IT & Networking Foundations Knowledge Check
description: Demonstration assessment exercising every supported question type and SCORM 2004 4th Edition interaction reporting.
author: SCORM Quiz Builder

settings.passMessage: Congratulations. You have demonstrated foundational IT and networking knowledge.
settings.failMessage: You did not reach 80%. Review the foundational modules and try again.

questions.prompt: In a star topology, how are devices connected?

options.label: Each device connects to a central switch or hub
options.feedback: Correct. The central node is the single point of connection.

options.label: Each device connects to two neighbors in a closed loop
All devices share a single backbone cable
Every device connects directly to every other device

questions.correctFeedback: Nice work identifying the star topology.
questions.rationale: A star topology centralizes connectivity through one switch or hub, simplifying troubleshooting.

questions.prompt: Which medium is least susceptible to electromagnetic interference?
questions.correctFeedback: Yes. Fiber uses light, so it is immune to EMI.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Copper media are affected by EMI; fiber is not.
questions.rationale: Fiber transmits light rather than electrical signals, eliminating EMI concerns.

questions.prompt: Select ALL layers that belong to the OSI model. (Partial credit applies.)
questions.partialFeedback: You identified some OSI layers. Cloud and Virtualization are not OSI layers.
questions.rationale: Physical, Transport, and Application are OSI layers; Cloud and Virtualization are not.

questions.prompt: Select the protocols that provide encryption. (Weighted scoring.)
questions.partialFeedback: At least one encrypted protocol identified.
questions.incorrectFeedback: HTTPS and SSH are the encrypted options.
questions.rationale: HTTPS and SSH encrypt traffic; HTTP and Telnet send data in clear text.

questions.prompt: Power over Ethernet (PoE) can deliver both data and electrical power over a single cable.
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. PoE carries data and power together.
questions.incorrectFeedback: PoE does carry both data and power.
questions.rationale: PoE injects DC power onto the same twisted pair used for data.

questions.prompt: Match each protocol to its default port. (Partial credit applies.)
questions.partialFeedback: Some ports matched. Review the common port list.
questions.rationale: HTTPS 443, SSH 22, DNS 53, HTTP 80 are the well-known defaults.

questions.prompt: Arrange these OSI layers from Layer 1 (bottom) to Layer 4. (Exact order required.)
questions.incorrectFeedback: The order is Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport.
questions.rationale: OSI layers 1 to 4 are Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport.

questions.prompt: How many usable host addresses are in a /24 IPv4 subnet?
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. 256 minus network and broadcast equals 254.
questions.rationale: 2^8 = 256 total addresses, minus the network and broadcast addresses.

questions.prompt: What three-letter acronym describes translating private IP addresses to a public IP address?
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. NAT translates private to public addressing.
questions.incorrectFeedback: The answer is NAT (Network Address Translation).
questions.rationale: NAT allows many private hosts to share one or more public addresses.

questions.prompt: Drag each device onto the OSI layer where it primarily operates. One item does not belong on either layer.
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Routers forward packets by IP address; switches and bridges forward frames by MAC address.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Review which address each device reads: IP (Layer 3) or MAC (Layer 2).
questions.rationale: A repeater only regenerates the signal, so it works at Layer 1 and belongs on neither layer.
